full_judgment: 5. The defendant-petitioners resisted the said application for temporary injunction by presenting a written objection traversing all the material allegations made in the plaint as well as the petition for temporary injunction contending inter alia that one pious Muslim built a Mosque during the Mughal period and dedicated the suit property in the name of "Allah". There was an Hujrakhana for the Imam of the Mosque and the Imam used to stay there. On the fall of Nabab Serajddoula the then East India Company for the education of the children of its English employees forcibly possessed the grave-yard and other land of the Mosque. During the cadastral Survey Record of Right .0784 acres of land stood recorded in the Khatian No. 8941 in the name of Moulvi Ibrahim, the Mutwalli. The stand taken by the defendants is that during the state Acquisition record of Right .0180 acres of land stood recorded in the name of the plaintiff school and the record of Right had been prepared by the plaintiff in collusion with the settlement officers. The defendant did never threaten the plaintiff, nor did attempt to enter into the suit property. The defendants assert that the plaintiff got no prima facie and arguable case in the matter of getting an order of injunction.
